knowledge:
- key_parameters: alpha=significance level for outlier detection boundaries ;; method=the outlier detection algorithm to use (e.g., "boxplot", "GESD", "medmad", "shorth") ;; scaling=a scaling function or multiplier for outlier boundaries depending on sample size and alpha ;; ftype=set to "ideal" for theoretical calibration of the boxplot rule ;; k=the number of possibly outlying points to prespecify in GESD (must be less than half the sample size)
- alternatives: Standard R boxplot visualization, which uses a fixed 1.5 IQR whisker rule without formal parametric calibration.
- when_to_use: Use when formal, calibrated statistical testing for outliers is required in univariate or multivariate genomic and general datasets, rather than relying on simple heuristic visualization thresholds.
- pitfalls: Specifying ftype="ideal" or using the "shorth" method may result in no data values falling in the outlier region, which triggers a warning and returns NA for indices and values. GESD requires a pre-specified maximum number of outliers (k) which must be carefully chosen.

workflows.name: univariate_outlier_detection
workflows.intent: Detect outliers in a univariate numeric vector using various parametric and resistant methods.
input: lead (a numeric vector of univariate measurements, such as tapping frequencies)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and define the univariate dataset ;; 2. Visualize the distribution using a standard boxplot ;; 3. Detect outliers using the boxplot method with custom scaling ;; 4. Detect outliers using the boxplot method with ideal calibration ;; 5. Detect outliers using the Generalized Extreme Studentized Deviate (GESD) procedure ;; 6. Detect outliers using the median and MAD (medmad) method with Hampel scaling ;; 7. Detect outliers using the shorth-based detector
workflows.code:
library(parody)
lead <- c(83, 70, 62, 55, 56, 57, 57, 58, 59, 50, 51, 
        52, 52, 52, 54, 54, 45, 46, 48,
        48, 49, 40, 40, 41, 42, 42, 44, 
        44, 35, 37, 38, 38, 34, 13, 14)
boxplot(lead)
calout.detect(lead,alpha=.05,method="boxplot", scaling=
function(n,alpha)1.5)
calout.detect(lead,alpha=.05,method="boxplot",ftype="ideal")
calout.detect(lead,alpha=.05,method="GESD",k=5)
calout.detect(lead,alpha=.05,method="medmad",scaling=hamp.scale.3)
calout.detect(lead,alpha=.05,method="shorth")

workflows.name: multivariate_outlier_detection
workflows.intent: Detect and visualize outliers in a multivariate dataset using Caroni and Prescott's generalized GESD method.
input: tcost (a multivariate data frame or matrix of numeric features)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the multivariate dataset ;; 2. Run multivariate outlier detection using mv.calout.detect ;; 3. Visualize identified outliers using a colored pairs plot ;; 4. Perform principal component analysis (PCA) and visualize with a biplot ;; 5. Remove identified outliers and re-run PCA to assess robustness
workflows.code:
data(tcost)
ostr = mv.calout.detect(tcost)
ostr
thecol = rep("black", nrow(tcost))
thecol[ostr$ind] = "red"
pairs(tcost, col=thecol, pch=19)
pc = prcomp(tcost)
biplot(pc)
ftcost = tcost[-c(9,21),]
fpc = prcomp(ftcost)
biplot(fpc)
